question: Why did the authors use a carbonate electrolyte with the sodium metal anode?

runs.text: The question's premise does not match the paper: the authors did not use a carbonate electrolyte. They deliberately avoided traditional carbonate electrolytes. Coin cells with sodium metal anodes were assembled with

support.quote: opposed to using traditional organic carbonate electrolytes

runs.text: instead, using NaPF6 salt dissolved in tetraglyme (a glyme-based electrolyte). The stated reason is that the glyme was chosen to overcome the unstable solid-electrolyte-interphase (SEI) formation on Na metal anodes that the authors observed in carbonate-based electrolytes.

support.quote: the unstable SEI formation on Na metal anodes observed in carbonate-based electrolytes

runs.text: The authors also state that a stable SEI on the sodium anode is critical to good cycling performance, and they built on earlier work showing sodium anode stability during reversible plating in glymes. In addition, the sulfur confinement strategy relies on a glyme-based electrolyte that gives a stable sodium-electrolyte interface.
